analysis.evidence: כֹל quantifies the singular שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה, “shrub of the field.” With טֶרֶם יִהְיֶה, “had yet to exist,” the clause means “and no shrub of the field yet existed on the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with prefixed conjunction וְ.

analysis.evidence: שִׂיחַ is in construct with הַשָּׂדֶה, giving “shrub of the field.” The parallel phrase עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה, “herb of the field,” and the explanation that rain had yet to fall identify it as vegetation.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun

analysis.evidence: In שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה, “shrub of the field,” הַשָּׂדֶה completes the construct phrase and identifies the shrub’s habitat. The parallel עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה, “herbage of the field,” supports the generic sense of open country.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: open country, the land outside town and house

analysis.evidence: טֶרֶם modifies יִהְיֶה in the first clause. No shrub of the field was yet present in the land. The parallel clause טֶרֶם יִצְמָח confirms this reading by describing growth that had yet to occur.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected temporal adverb with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: טֶרֶם יִהְיֶה בָאָרֶץ says that no shrub of the field was yet present on the earth. טֶרֶם supplies “not yet,” and בָאָרֶץ gives the location. The parallel clause uses יִצְמָח for the distinct act of sprouting.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with שִׂיחַ.

analysis.evidence: בָאָרֶץ tells where no shrub of the field was yet growing. The parallel clause about field plants that had yet to sprout and the explanation that rain had yet to fall identify the ground as the surface where vegetation grows.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article, prefixed to a common noun, singular absolute, of common gender.

analysis.evidence: וְכָל quantifies עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה, “plant of the field.” With טֶרֶם יִצְמָח, “had not yet sprouted,” the clause means “and no plant of the field had yet sprouted.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed conjunction וְ.

analysis.evidence: In עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה, “grass of the field,” הַשָּׂדֶה completes the construct phrase. טֶרֶם יִצְמָח says that the grass had yet to sprout.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה, “vegetation of the field,” the marked noun identifies where the vegetation grows. The parallel phrase שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה, “shrub of the field,” uses the same noun for the same setting.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הַ.
analysis.sense: open country, the land outside town and house

analysis.evidence: טֶרֶם modifies יִצְמָח, indicating that the vegetation of the field had not yet sprouted. This parallels טֶרֶם יִהְיֶה in the preceding clause.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected temporal adverb without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: יִצְמָח agrees with the masculine singular עֵשֶׂב ‘vegetation’. With טֶרֶם ‘not yet’, the clause says that no vegetation of the field had yet sprouted. The following clause explains that rain had not yet fallen.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason the field vegetation had not yet appeared or sprouted: לֹא הִמְטִיר יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָרֶץ, “YHWH God had not sent rain upon the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected causal conjunction without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 2:25 as an example under the existing Hebrew sense “not (of a fact)” in lo.
draft.definition: Before a verb, לֹא denies that its subject does or experiences what the verb expresses.
draft.evidence: Genesis 2:25 uses וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ, “and they were not ashamed”, to describe the man and his wife.

analysis.evidence: In כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר, לֹא negates הִמְטִיר. The clause explains why vegetation had yet to sprout. YHWH God had not caused rain to fall on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: לֹא negates הִמְטִיר. The subject is יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, and עַל הָאָרֶץ identifies where the rain would fall. The clause explains why the field plants had yet to sprout.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular, with no attached prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, ‘because Yahweh God had not sent rain,’ יַהְוֶה names the subject of הִמְטִיר, with אֱלֹהִים in apposition.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים, אֱלֹהִים identifies Yahweh as God. The singular verb הִמְטִיר presents him as the one who had not yet caused rain to fall on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לֹא הִמְטִיר יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל introduces הָאָרֶץ as the surface on which YHWH God had yet to send rain.
analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל הָאָרֶץ, the ground is the surface on which rain had yet to fall. The clause explains why the field plants had yet to grow.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, common gender.

analysis.evidence: וְאָדָם אַיִן means “and there was no one.” The infinitive לַעֲבֹד and its object אֶת־הָאֲדָמָה specify the task for which no one was present, “to till the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun without the article.
analysis.sense: a man, a human being; anyone

analysis.evidence: In וְאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, אַיִן follows its subject אָדָם and expresses absence: “there was no human to till the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Negative existential particle in the absolute form, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: there is no, there is not

analysis.evidence: וְאָדָם אַיִן means “there was no one,” and לַעֲבֹד specifies the task for which a person was lacking. The direct object אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground,” gives עָבַד its agricultural sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed preposition לַ־

analysis.evidence: In לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, “to till the ground,” אֶת marks the definite noun הָאֲדָמָה as the direct object of לַעֲבֹד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object marker without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה, “to till the ground,” אֶת marks הָאֲדָמָה as the direct object. The verse says there was no one to cultivate the soil.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: the ground that is tilled; soil
